title: BBC Apologizes After Inappropriate Audio Interrupts Strictly Live Show
excerpt:
An inappropriate recording disrupted the live Strictly Come Dancing broadcast in Blackpool.
The BBC apologized and police are investigating the incident.
body_md:
A live broadcast of the BBC dance competition Strictly Come Dancing was disrupted by an unexpected and inappropriate sound at Blackpool's Tower Ballroom. Judge Motsi Mabuse was commenting on a performance by Delta Goodrem and her dance partner Kai Widdrington when microphones picked up a noise apparently coming from the audience. According to the report, it sounded as though a recording of sexual noises had been played, although the precise origin had not been conclusively established.

Mabuse briefly turned toward the audience to understand what was happening, then faced the camera and made clear that she was not responsible. The interruption unfolded during a live television production, where unwanted audio can reach viewers before a production team has an opportunity to respond. Strictly is one of Britain's best-known dance competitions and the format that inspired the American Dancing with the Stars.

At the end of the broadcast, presenter Emma Willis apologized to viewers who might have heard the audio disruption. A BBC spokesperson subsequently issued a separate apology to anyone offended during the live show and said the broadcaster was investigating how the incident occurred. The broadcaster's response therefore extended beyond the brief on-air exchange.

Lancashire Police also confirmed that officers were aware of an incident during filming in Blackpool. Police said they had been in contact with event organizers, a formal complaint had been made, and a mobile phone had been seized. Investigators were considering whether any criminal offenses had occurred. Neither the seizure of a device nor the existence of a complaint establishes who caused the disruption or whether a crime was committed.

The incident recalls a similar interruption to a BBC live sports broadcast in 2023. During coverage of a football match between Wolves and Liverpool, presenter Gary Lineker was distracted by comparable noises. He later shared a picture of a phone that he said had been attached behind the studio set, apparently as part of a prank. The earlier event provides context but does not prove that the same method was used at Strictly.

For now, the confirmed facts are the on-air disturbance, the BBC's apology and the police inquiry. The identity and motivation of any person responsible, and the eventual outcome of the investigation, remain unconfirmed.
